summary: Lists the VPIM email address formats in common use and defines some new ones for special cases, and sets requirements for addresses in VPIM submission mode.

eli5.summary: This describes the different ways to write the address of a voicemail box so messages find it.

subtitle: How to write email addresses that point at voice mailboxes, outdialing devices and AMIS voice networks.

tldr.problem: Voice mail systems identify mailboxes with telephone numbers, but VPIM v2 puts no restrictions on email address format and simple systems cannot resolve phone numbers into routable addresses.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC builds on GSTN address formats to define service selectors (VPIM, VOICE, AMIS, plus fax) that go in the left side of an email address, so a submission gateway knows how to deliver a message to a phone number.
tldr.outcome: VPIM and IVM systems that support submission MUST accept, translate and forward messages sent to these addresses, and new GSTN registrations were requested from IANA.

today: RFC 3804 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is a companion to RFC 3801, which defines VPIM version 2.

sections.title: Why VPIM Needs Address Rules
sections.content:
The Voice Profile for Internet Mail version 2 (RFC 2421) does not restrict the email address format. It does recommend a numeric left-hand side (LHS, the part before the @) because many legacy voice mail systems identify mailboxes only by digits. The private format has become deployed in most existing VPIM v2 systems, and some systems only accept messages from addresses with a numeric LHS.

The Internet Voice Mail (IVM) specification does not describe addressing at all. It is useful in some cases, such as submission or tunneling, to specify an LHS format, so a format based on GSTN addressing is presented. This document defines the various recipient (TO) addresses for VPIM and IVM messages.
sections.eli5: Voice mailboxes use phone numbers, and email uses names with an at-sign. This document says how to mix the two so messages find the right box.

sections.title: VPIM v2 Addressing and General Rules
sections.content:
VPIM v2 addressing is defined in section 4.1.1 of RFC 2421 and RFC 3801. Of its four address groups, the mailbox number format is the most commonly used, for example 6137637582@nortelnetworks.com.

For VPIM in general there are no restrictions on the form of the Internet address. VPIM systems must be able to receive an arbitrary email address and generate a reply to it, so no inferences about the structure of the local part should be necessary. Recipient addresses must be compatible with the recipient's system and consistent with the address entry capabilities of a telephone user interface. The syntax is written in ABNF.
sections.eli5: Normal voice mail addresses are mostly a phone number then an at-sign and a company name. A machine must be able to reply to whatever address it gets, even a strange one.

sections.title: Gateways and the Submission Idea
sections.content:
A gateway translates between dissimilar environments. A VPIM gateway connects the VPIM profile of Internet mail with other voice mail networking protocols, proprietary or standard (like AMIS). An onramp connects from another voice mail networking protocol to VPIM, and an offramp connects from VPIM to another one. Their behavior is out of scope; the RFC describes only the VPIM service portion of their addressing.

Limited capability voice mail machines may send messages by default to an external message submission gateway, which converts the unresolved telephone number of the recipient into a legitimate email address. Limited email systems may likewise send to a VPIM onramp named on the right-hand side (RHS), with the LHS saying the message goes as VPIM to the telephone number given. Telephone numbers in submission mode MUST use one of the forms below, based on GSTN-ADDR (RFC 3191) and the extensions in RFC 2846.
sections.eli5: A gateway is a translator at a border. A simple machine can hand over just a phone number, and the translator turns it into a proper address and sends it on.

sections.title: VPIM, VOICE and AMIS Address Forms
sections.content:
Each form starts with a service selector. For VPIM messages it is VPIM. A vpim-mbox is an optional VPIM= prefix and a phone number, with an optional extension and distribution list. The extension form is /EXT= (or +, kept for compatibility with VPIM v2 addressing) and the list form is /DL=; both keywords are case insensitive. Examples: VPIM=6137637582, VPIM=7035255550/EXT=227 for a mailbox behind a non-ISDN PBX, and VPIM=+14165977230/DL=93 for a distribution list.

For a voice outdialing at the destination system the selector is VOICE, and the mailbox needs the VOICE= prefix, for example VOICE=+3940226338.

For AMIS (Audio Messaging Interchange Specification) messages the selector is AMIS, with an optional /SYSNUM= part, also case insensitive. The AMIS mailbox is AMIS-A or AMIS-D style. A PSTN number is limited to 15 numeric digits per ITU E.164, a private number to 14 digits, and the AMIS-D field to 32 characters. The + separators replace the hash-sign separators of AMIS-A. Example: AMIS=+1/401+3278144+/SYSNUM=1+401+3279542+.

Fax addresses are formatted as defined in section 2 of RFC 3192.
sections.eli5: The first word tells the machine what to do: VPIM means store it as voice mail, VOICE means ring the phone and play it, and AMIS means pass it to an older voice network.

sections.title: Submission Email Addresses
sections.content:
The full email addresses are built from the LHS forms above. VPIM and IVM systems that support submission MUST accept, translate if necessary, and forward messages sent to these addresses.

Each has the shape ["/"] address ["/"] "@" mta-I-pstn. The vpim-email usually points to a VPIM capable messaging system that delivers the attached message. The voice-email usually points to a device that makes a telephone call to the number and plays a voice attachment. The amis-email usually points to a gateway to an AMIS network. Fax email addresses follow section 4 of RFC 3192.
sections.eli5: Put the phone-number part before the at-sign and the name of a helper machine after it. The helper machine then does the real delivery.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Most security considerations are already identified in RFC 2421 and the IVM document. An additional concern is that the sender must trust, and be aware of the policies of, the submission MTA, because that MTA decides the final destination and how to deliver based on the submission LHS.

Submission MTAs should take care not to blindly place outdial calls to any number submitted, for example international numbers or 1-900 numbers. Ideally, senders should be authenticated to confirm their outdialing privileges.
sections.eli5: If a machine will phone anyone for you, strangers could make it call expensive numbers. So it should check who is asking first.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
The RFC includes registration forms for new GSTN address values. Three are service selectors: VPIM (a voice mailbox that accepts a VPIM message), VOICE (a voice device sent a message by outdialing) and AMIS (a mailbox sent an AMIS voice mail message).

Three are qualif-type1 keywords. sysnum (digits and +) is the optional AMIS sub-address, restricted to the AMIS selector. ext (digits) identifies a particular VPIM mailbox, and dl (digits) is a personal distribution list for a VPIM mailbox. The last two are intended for the VPIM selector but may be used outside it.
sections.eli5: New words were added to an official dictionary of address words so everyone spells them the same way.

items.desc: For a mailbox without a direct dial number.

items.desc: A list tied to a phone number.
